input.summary: Meridian's vendor portfolio spans seven active platforms with unresolved contract risk and no governed integration path to the target lakehouse.
covers: Legacy analytics estate (Tableau, SAS, SQL Marts)
AI and productivity tooling (Microsoft, Genesys, Salesforce)
Executive use-case demand vs. vendor readiness gap
sources: Synthetic PHI-free planning-grade context — not real Meridian production data

story.meaning: Meridian carries a fragmented vendor portfolio where legacy analytics spend (Tableau, SAS, SQL Marts) is structurally misaligned with the AWS/Databricks target state, and no vendor contract is yet positioned to deliver a governed lakehouse.
story.observed: Seven active vendors are evidenced. Epic, Microsoft, Tableau, SAS, and an outsourced managed services provider sustain current-state operations. AWS and Databricks are contracted as target direction but lack a certified medallion architecture or analytics-ready foundation. The managed services provider absorbs an estimated 80% maintenance load, leaving minimal capacity for net-new delivery.
story.matters: Every top-five executive use case — lakehouse, AI/LLM governance, cost transparency, payment integrity, call center optimization — requires vendor decisions that cannot reach decision grade until contract terms, integration evidence, and governance controls are certified. Delay compounds technical debt and defers value realization.
story.supports: Nexus vendor dimension provides the contract risk map and evidence gate status that procurement, CIO, and CDAO need to sequence vendor negotiations and platform investments against use-case readiness.

findings: Epic's Clarity and Caboodle integration to a governed lakehouse is unproven — the single largest clinical data blocker across four of five priority use cases.
The outsourced analytics managed services provider's ~80% maintenance load structurally limits net-new delivery capacity, creating a hidden program risk for every AI initiative.

AWS and Databricks are target-state direction only — no certified medallion architecture, no analytics-ready foundation, and no commercial terms are yet evidenced, making all lakehouse timelines aspirational.
SAS model lineage is ungoverned; Tableau extract sprawl is uncontrolled — both must be rationalized before payment integrity and cost transparency use cases can advance to decision grade.

chain: vendors → data_platforms (Epic Clarity/Caboodle feeds lakehouse foundation)
vendors → use_cases (contract readiness gates all five priority use cases)

relationships.note: Vendor contract risk is the upstream gate for platform, governance, and use-case dimensions — no use case reaches decision grade until Epic integration, AWS/Databricks foundation, and managed services scope are resolved and commercially evidenced.

evidence.name: Epic Vendor Record
evidence.facts: Epic provides clinical EHR (Hyperspace), reporting (Clarity), and analytics (Caboodle). Integration to a governed lakehouse is unproven. Contract pricing not yet evidenced.
evidence.supports: Clinical data foundation for lakehouse and provider quality use cases
evidence.missing: Lakehouse integration design, medallion mapping, and commercial terms

evidence.name: AWS + Databricks Vendor Records
evidence.facts: AWS and Databricks are designated target-state cloud and lakehouse platforms. No certified medallion architecture. No analytics-ready foundation. Commercial terms not evidenced.
evidence.supports: Target platform direction for all five priority use cases
evidence.missing: Medallion architecture certification, foundation readiness evidence, and commercial terms

evidence.name: Outsourced Analytics Managed Services Provider Record
evidence.facts: Provider absorbs estimated 80% maintenance load across SQL Marts, Tableau, Power BI, and SAS. Vendor identity and contract values not yet evidenced. Limits net-new delivery capacity.
evidence.fields: vendor_id, service, owning_function, linked_systems, contract_risk, pricing_basis
evidence.supports: CDAO operating model and capacity planning
evidence.missing: Vendor identity, SOW scope, FTE split, and contract values

evidence.name: Tableau + SAS Vendor Records
evidence.facts: Tableau carries extract sprawl and duplicate dashboard risk. SAS model and extract lineage is ungoverned. Both block payment integrity and cost transparency use cases from advancing.
evidence.supports: Legacy analytics rationalization and payment integrity use case
evidence.missing: Rationalization roadmap, model lineage inventory, and commercial terms

evidence.name: CEO / CIO / CFO Stakeholder Intent Signals — Vendor-Linked Use Cases
evidence.facts: CEO, CFO, and CIO all flag lakehouse, AI/LLM governance, call center optimization, cost transparency, and payment integrity as top priorities. All are blocked pending vendor evidence closure. No use case is decision-grade.
evidence.supports: Executive demand signal for vendor sequencing and contract prioritization
evidence.missing: Decision-grade evidence gates for each use case; vendor contract terms required before sourcing events

evidence.name: AI Vendor Signals (Microsoft Copilot, Genesys, Salesforce)
evidence.facts: Microsoft M365 Copilot, Genesys, and Salesforce are referenced across AI, contact center, and CRM use cases. HITL, audit logging, and model-risk controls are not yet evidenced for any AI-enabled vendor.
evidence.supports: AI Governance / Model Risk Controls and Contact Center Optimization use cases
evidence.missing: HITL controls, AI audit trail, OneTrust/Purview integration confirmation, and CISO sign-off
